assignment.review_focus: MATRIX-001 — Design input to output parameter consistency for PT9L. Verify that key design-input parameters (measurement range, accuracy, response time, environmental conditions, Bluetooth specification, intended-use population, forehead measurement site) stated in the design input document (PT9L-KHXQ01 or equivalent) are carried forward without alteration or omission into design output documents (drawings, specifications, verification/validation test conditions). Flag any parameter value, unit, or scope discrepancy between design input and output layers. Also check whether PT9C PCB sub-component parameters are correctly scoped to PT9L system-level requirements rather than being inherited verbatim from a PT9C standalone specification.

mandatory_audit_matrix.check_goal: Verify that key PT9L design-input parameters are carried into design outputs and validation conditions consistently.

assignment.review_focus: MATRIX-001 — Design input to output parameter consistency for PT9L. Verify that key design-input parameters (measurement range, accuracy, response time, environmental conditions, Bluetooth specification, intended-use population, forehead measurement site) stated in the design input document (PT9L-KHXQ01 or equivalent) are carried forward without alteration or omission into design output documents (drawings, specifications, verification/validation test conditions). Flag any parameter value, unit, or scope discrepancy between design input and output layers. Also check whether PT9C PCB sub-component parameters are correctly scoped to PT9L system-level requirements rather than being inherited verbatim from a PT9C standalone specification.

agent_runs.summary: Cross-corpus scan of the PT9L DHF/DMR package reveals 14 candidate consistency issues spanning legacy product residue in active documents, document-number mismatches, unsigned approvals, wrong-product references in BOM and label documents, regulatory applicability conflicts, software diagram contamination, and blood-pressure-specific language appearing in a thermometer DHF.

llm_output.summary: Hardware audit of PT9L DHF/DMR reveals five substantive consistency findings: a blood-pressure residue phrase in the battery design-verification plan/report, an unresolved BOM conflict between PT3-P10 dual-spring and PT5-M02/M03 separate springs, a total-assembly drawing part-number anomaly (T-Z1-P10 used for two distinct PCBs), missing pass/fail verdicts in multiple T1 sample review checklists, and object-temperature mode accuracy tolerance (±0.2 °C) applied at 30 °C and 45 °C in software test plans despite the design-input accuracy specification only requiring ±0.2 °C for ≥35 °C and ≤42 °C.
review_notes: Measurement accuracy specification ≥35 °C and ≤42 °C: ±0.2 °C; outside that range: ±0.3 °C is consistently stated across design input (HW-003), product inspection standard (HW-035), design verification plan (HW-056), design verification report (HW-051), product overview (HW-063), and defect definition (HW-064). No discrepancy found for body-temperature mode accuracy.
Measurement range 32 °C–42.9 °C stated in label audit (HW-024, HW-025) and operation guide (HW-034) is consistent with each other.
PCB design review checklist items (HW-004 through HW-009) all show 'pass' verdicts; no anomaly found in those items.
Battery polarity marking confirmed present in label audit (HW-023, HW-028); battery removal warning confirmed in operation guide (HW-026, HW-029).

Low-battery software requirement (HW-060) and battery-voltage sampling function (HW-044, HW-059) are present; no explicit low-voltage cutoff threshold value was found in the supplied evidence to cross-check against a hardware specification, so no finding is raised on threshold value alone.
PCB part number PT9L-HFMP01 V1.0 is consistently referenced across EBOM (HW-040, HW-077), T1 BOM (HW-042), SMT instruction (HW-062), and design output list (HW-079 through HW-084).

PT9C-CNTP01 V1.0 sensor PCB appears in EBOM (HW-041, HW-078) and T1 BOM (HW-043); its presence as a sub-component is noted but no standalone PT9C accuracy specification was supplied in evidence to compare against PT9L system-level requirements, so a separate finding is not raised beyond what is observable.
ASTM accuracy reference in operation guide (HW-031) cites ±0.2 °C for 37–39 °C range for IR thermometers, which is consistent with the design-input accuracy requirement for the clinical range.

findings.claim: The design verification plan and one section of the design verification report for the PT9L thermometer contain the phrase '次血压测量' (blood pressure measurements) in the rechargeable-battery capacity requirement, which is a blood-pressure-monitor residue that does not apply to a thermometer and creates a traceability break between the design input and the verification documents.
findings.rationale: HW-002 (design input, F0031) states the battery requirement as '□可充电电池：在充满电后，电池电量至少能进行 次测量' using the generic word '测量' (measurements). HW-058 (design verification plan, F0121) and HW-055 (design verification report section, F0114 line 110) both replace '测量' with '血压测量' (blood pressure measurements). HW-053 (design verification report, F0114 line 54) correctly uses '测量' without the blood-pressure qualifier, showing the error is not universal but is present in at least two documents. This inconsistency means the verification plan and one report section are tracing to a wrong-product requirement.
challenge_questions: Which document version control step introduced '血压测量' into the PT9L verification plan and report, and has a formal correction or deviation been raised?

Is there a separate battery-life test report referenced in HW-053 ('电池使用寿命测试报告') that also contains the blood-pressure phrase, and if so, does it affect the validity of the battery verification conclusion?
Has the design verification plan (F0121) been reviewed and approved after the '血压测量' phrase was introduced, and by whom?

findings.claim: The software test plan and test record apply an accuracy tolerance of ±0.2 °C to object-temperature mode measurements at 30 °C and 45 °C blackbody targets, but the design-input accuracy specification only mandates ±0.2 °C for the body-temperature range ≥35 °C and ≤42 °C; outside that range the requirement is ±0.3 °C, so the test plan imposes a tighter-than-specified tolerance at 30 °C and 45 °C without documented justification.
findings.rationale: HW-003 (F0031, design input) and HW-035 (F0090, inspection standard) both state: '≥35 °C and ≤42 °C: ±0.2 °C; other: ±0.3 °C.' HW-045 and HW-046 (F0101, software test plan lines 343–344) specify acceptance criteria of '30±0.2 °C' and '45±0.2 °C' for object-temperature mode blackbody tests. HW-048 and HW-049 (F0102, software test record lines 68–69) repeat the same ±0.2 °C criteria at 30 °C and 45 °C. Since 30 °C and 45 °C are outside the ≥35–42 °C range, the design input would permit ±0.3 °C at those points. Applying ±0.2 °C is more stringent than required; if units fail at ±0.2 °C but pass at ±0.3 °C, the test plan would incorrectly reject conforming product, or alternatively the tighter tolerance represents an undocumented design intent that has not been captured in the design input.
challenge_questions: Is the ±0.2 °C tolerance at 30 °C and 45 °C in the software test plan an intentional tighter requirement for object-temperature mode, and if so, has it been formally documented as a design input or design output specification?
Were any units rejected during software testing at 30 °C or 45 °C that would have passed under the ±0.3 °C design-input tolerance, and how were those dispositioned?

Should the design input (HW-003) be updated to separately specify accuracy requirements for object-temperature mode versus body-temperature mode, or should the test plan be corrected to use ±0.3 °C outside the 35–42 °C range?
